shelfmark: UTO Sinai Syriac NF M 56, SPP No. 335
fol: Reconstructed folio order, ff. 12v, 1r, 12r, 1v, 23v, 14r, 23r, 14v, 50v, 55r, 50r, 55v, 28v, 27r, 28r, 27v, 29v, 26r, 29r, 26v, 49v, 56r, 49r, 56v, 53v, 52r, 53r, 52v, 110av, 110ar, 54v, 51r, 54r, 51v, 72v, 69r, 72r, 69v, 71v, 70r, 71r, 70v, 25r, 29bv, 25v, 29br, 25ar, 29av, 25av, 29ar, 48r, 57v, 48v, 57r, 20v, 17r, 20r, 17v, 19v, 18r, 19r, 18v, 47r, 58v, 47v, 58r ~ Every extant folio is either the upper half or the bottom part of one original folio which was folded to constitute the actual quires.

layer_record.label: Sinai Syriac NF M 56, Undertext (Christian Palestinian Aramaic)

note: Ancient calligraphy | Alaph: apex as crochet-hook shape ("en crochet à dentelle") ; Beth, dalath, resh, mim: extremity with drop shape (extrémité "en goutte") ; Gamal, teth, lamadh: heron shape ("en tête de héron") ; Heth: H with curved uprights and horizontal hyphen ; Kaph: duck head shape ("en tête de canard") ; Nun: nail head shape ("en tête de clou") ; some Nun final on last line: ornamented tail as a spiral
Column width: 6.2-6.4 cm; distance between columns: 1.9-2 cm; line spacing: 0.8-0.9 cm; medium height of letters: 0.4 cm; height of initial waw: 0.7 cm; height of lamad and taw: 0.4 cm
Visible ruling on some folios: the 4 vertical and all the horizontal plus a line above line 1. Pricking corresponding to each line

bib.citation: Lewis, Agnes Smith and Margaret Dunlop Gibson. The Palestinian Syriac Lectionary of the Gospels. London: 1899
note: Re-edited from two Sinai Mss and from P. de Lagarde’s edition of the Evangeliarium Hierosolymitanum

cataloguer.message: Description and identification of undertexts as part of SPP (2011-2016). Migrated to SMDL in 2025.

program.label: Sinai Palimpsests Project
program.description: Imaged and studied as part of the Sinai Palimpsests Project (2011–2016), a collaboration between St. Catherine’s Monastery of the Sinai, the Early Manuscripts Electronic Library, and UCLA Library, funded by the Arcadia Fund and the Ahmanson Foundation. The project used multispectral imaging and scholarly analysis to recover and document erased and obscured texts in palimpsest manuscripts from the monastery’s collection.

note.value: The UTO Gospel of Matthew belonged to the same original manuscript

Quire numbers on bottom margin on some folios, signatures "en miroir" (mirror quire signature) as usual in CPA manuscripts; quires of 8 folios (quaternion); organization of parchment sheets: always flesh facing flesh and hair facing hair (according rule of Gregory)
